firmographic.name: Resend
firmographic.company_description:
Resend is a developer-focused email API platform founded in 2023 in San Francisco that provides transactional and marketing email infrastructure through a REST API and nine official SDKs (Node.js, Python, Ruby, PHP, Laravel, Go, Rust, Java, .NET), an SMTP service, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server enabling AI agent integration. The platform's core architecture includes multi-region sending from North America, Europe (Ireland), and South America (Brazil) to reduce delivery latency, fully managed dedicated IPs with automatic warm-up, modular webhooks for email lifecycle events, batch sending (up to 100 emails per request) with idempotency keys, scheduled sends up to 72 hours, and an inbound email processing layer. Resend's differentiator centers on developer experience: React Email is an open-source React component library that replaces legacy table-based HTML email templates, and the company publishes migration guides, knowledge-base content, and SDKs that position documentation as part of the product.

The revenue model is a hybrid of usage-based per-email pricing with monthly volume tiers (3,000 emails free, 50,000 at $20/mo, 100,000 at $35/mo, 1,000,000 at $650/mo), a $30/month dedicated IP add-on, subscription tiers (Free, Pro, Scale), and custom annual enterprise contracts with dedicated Slack channels and deliverability consulting. Pricing sits materially below legacy incumbents — at 100,000 emails/month Resend charges $35 versus Postmark's $115. Go-to-market combines self-serve product-led growth (no credit card required for free tier), developer community and content marketing (React Email open source, Resend Forward conference, Insiders ambassador program, hackathons), and an enterprise overlay with founding account executives targeting high-volume senders. Named customers span high-growth developer-tool startups (Vercel, Replit, Gumroad, Outerbase, Infisical) and large enterprises (eBay, Warner Bros, MrBeast/Beast Industries, A24, Valentino, Max, Tailwind CSS). Resend has raised $21 million across a $3M seed round (July 2023, Y Combinator and SV Angel) and an $18M Series A (December 2024, led by Andreessen Horowitz), and acquired Mergent (infrastructure management) in April 2025 and Briefer (data notebooks) in August 2025, indicating a strategic push beyond pure email into broader developer infrastructure.
firmographic.company_description_short: Resend is a developer-focused email API platform founded in 2023 that provides transactional and marketing email infrastructure via REST API and nine SDKs, serving software engineers, high-growth startups, and enterprises with React Email templates, multi-region sending, and managed dedicated IPs.

recent_move.description: Closed $18 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), bringing total disclosed funding to $21M and providing growth capital for product expansion and enterprise GTM.
Acquired Briefer, a data notebook platform, expanding Resend's portfolio beyond email into interactive data exploration and visualization.

Launched the Enterprise plan with dedicated Slack channels, critical-severity ticket support, domain expert access, and custom migration services, formalizing an upmarket GTM motion.

expansion_highlight.description: Two completed acquisitions in 2025 — Mergent (April 23, 2025, infrastructure management) and Briefer (August 5, 2025, data notebooks) — signal a deliberate platform expansion beyond pure email into adjacent developer infrastructure. The pace and sequencing suggest an active inorganic growth strategy post Series A.

Inbound Emails (November 2025), Automations (2026), MCP Server (2025), Resend CLI / CLI 2.0 (2026), Schedule Email API (August 2024), Deliverability Insights (August 2024), Scale plan (October 2024), and Enterprise plan (2024) collectively broaden the platform from a send-only API into a full email communications suite (receive, automate, broadcast, schedule, analyze).

Launch of an explicit Enterprise plan (2024) with dedicated Slack channels, critical ticket severity, and domain expert access indicates upmarket movement. Hiring of two Founding Account Executives (Aneil Singh, Trey Knowles), a GTM Engineer (Sophia Faria), and a Recruiter (Areia Spinner) confirms field-sales buildout targeting Fortune-class logos.

Multi-region sending infrastructure currently spans North America (Virginia), Europe (Ireland), and South America (Brazil); the company website also references Asian region support. Operating geographies formally listed as North America, Europe, South America, and Asia. Geographic expansion is co-evolving with multi-region latency/durability positioning.

Beyond Founding AEs and GTM Engineer, the team expanded across customer success engineering (Anna Ward, Brian Kerr, Pauline Chin, Jp Valery, Slater Smith, Evan Thibodeau), developer experience (Chris Pennington, Christina Martinez, Haison Ohara), software engineering (Felipe Volpone, ex-Red Hat / iFood staff engineer), and product design (Zeh Fernandes). A dedicated Recruiter hire signals headcount scaling beyond founder-led hiring.

MCP Server for AI agents, Agent Skills documentation, Agent Onboarding guides, and integration partnerships (Novu, Knock, Trigger.dev, Pipedream, Supabase, Auth0, n8n, Zapier, Paper, Playwright) indicate deliberate ecosystem and channel-partner expansion to make Resend the default email layer across adjacent platforms.
